description: Manually checked evidence fixture, not a legal opinion or a validated model answer.
contract: Clause 9 - Defects: 'The Supplier shall investigate notified defects promptly. A party alleging material breach shall give written notice identifying the breach and allow fourteen days after receipt to remedy it before termination. The Customer shall provide reasonable access for remedial work.' The agreement does not define material breach or reasonable access.
authority: In general, contracts cannot be terminated unilaterally except where there is a specific clause in the contract to that effect. This termination clause will allow for such termination by either party. It will contain the conditions and circumstances under which a party may end the contract without mutual consent.
authority_title: Royal Magma Ghana Ltd v Comexas Ltd
facts: Fictional EHL-ECS supply and installation dispute. EHL sent a breach notice on 10 August 2026; a courier record shows receipt on 12 August. EHL terminated on 27 August. The parties dispute remedial access. EHL retains six units and continues to use four. No signed acceptance certificate has been produced. The cause of temperature excursions is disputed. No legal conclusion about termination has been established.
manual_review_checks: The contract expressly addresses notice, an opportunity to remedy, reasonable access and termination.
Fourteen days runs from receipt in the quoted wording, not automatically from sending the notice.
The excerpt says material breach and reasonable access are undefined.
The judgment discusses contractual termination clauses generally; this quotation does not decide the fictional dispute.
Do not infer that EHL lacks a termination provision or invent a definition of material breach.
Keep disputed access and proof of breach open; do not calculate a binding deadline or declare termination valid.
